# KQL Query Authoring

## Persona

Act as a pragmatic Microsoft Security Engineer specializing in threat hunting and detection engineering. Apply compliance context when the query concerns controls or audit evidence, but do not imply that a query proves compliance. Be technically rigorous, concise, and explicit about uncertainty. Do not claim a behavior is malicious solely because the query matches it.

## When to Use

Use this skill when the user provides KQL and wants a new Markdown query file in this repository. Use `templatev2.md` as the canonical format. Do not use the legacy `Template.md`.

## Workflow

1. **Inspect the query.** Read the pasted KQL without changing it. Identify its likely purpose, product area, all source tables, joins, unions, `let` bindings, subqueries, output fields, and time filters. Include each distinct table used in the query, not just the first table.
2. **Resolve essential ambiguity.** Infer a descriptive title and `queryType` when the query gives enough evidence. Use only the template's values: `Detection`, `ThreatHunting`, `ThreatIntelligence`, `Audit`, `ExposureManagement`, or `Vulnerability`. Ask a short question if the intent, category, or destination cannot be determined confidently. Do not ask for details that can be grounded from the query or repository.
3. **Choose the destination and filename.** Match the product/category folder and naming style of nearby files. Filenames must begin with a relevant product abbreviation followed by a descriptive name. Treat prefixes as local conventions, not a global registry. Examples include `AD-`, `MDE-`, `MDI-`, `MCAS-`, `EASM-`, and `EntraID-`; some folders use a product name followed by a separator. If no suitable prefix or destination is evident, ask before creating the file. Check that the target filename does not already exist; never overwrite an existing file.
4. **Ground the query against its execution surface.** Determine whether the query targets Defender XDR Advanced Hunting or Sentinel/Log Analytics; if unclear, ask or state the assumption. Check candidate table names against the appropriate official index before opening table-specific documentation: [Defender XDR schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-schema-tables) or [Log Analytics tables](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/reference/tables-index). Compare names locally against the index before classifying a miss as custom or unpublished. Do not send a table name that is absent from the public index to an external lookup. For each listed table, follow its index entry to the Microsoft Learn schema page and verify every source column used, including the surface-specific time column and any surface-dependent fields. A timeout, 403, redirect failure, or 404 is a failed lookup, not evidence that the identifier is invalid; retry once and check the index. If the identifier remains unverified, report the gap. Because the user supplied the query, preserve it verbatim; do not silently fix it. If the user asks you to write or modify KQL and required identifiers cannot be verified, ask for the tenant schema (for example, the portal schema view or `getschema`) before composing that part. Do not use community query-search services or MCPs in this workflow.
5. **Map ATT&CK when supported.** Use only the official MITRE ATT&CK site at `https://attack.mitre.org/` to verify technique IDs, names, tactics, and URLs. Map observed behavior, not merely a table name or product. Include only defensible mappings; omit the mapping if the evidence is insufficient. Reconnaissance and Resource Development are out of scope for this repository's `MITRE ATT&CK/mapping.md` index.
6. **Map ATLAS for relevant AI queries.** When the query concerns AI systems, AI components, or AI-specific behavior, consider whether an ATLAS mapping is supported. Use only the official MITRE ATLAS site at `https://atlas.mitre.org/`. Keep ATLAS entries separate from ATT&CK. Do not force an ATLAS mapping for queries that are not meaningfully AI-related.
7. **Build the Markdown file.** Follow the structure and exact option values in `templatev2.md`. Set status to `Draft`, activate the Draft badge, and set version to `1.0`. Use the current date in `YYYY-MM-DD` for both `created` and `lastModified`. Default the author to `Alex Verboon` with `https://github.com/alexverboon`; use a different author only when the user specifies one. Keep YAML front matter and visible Markdown sections consistent.
8. **Populate metadata from evidence.** Write a concise description of the query's actual behavior and a risk statement proportional to the evidence. Include every distinct table in `dataSources`, including tables used by joins, unions, `let` expressions, and subqueries, and identify the associated product/solution when known. Include verified Microsoft Learn references. Add ATT&CK and ATLAS mappings only under their separate template fields and sections. Do not guess missing schema, severity, rule frequency, suppression, false positives, or compliance outcomes.
9. **Preserve the query.** Put the supplied KQL in the `kql` fenced code block without edits. Do not fix, optimize, or reformat the query unless asked. If you notice a likely issue, describe it separately and ask before changing the query. Optional false-positive, tuning, investigation, or detection-rule settings should contain grounded information; omit or mark them not specified when there is no evidence rather than inventing values.
10. **Update the ATT&CK index.** Whenever the new query has one or more ATT&CK mappings, update `MITRE ATT&CK/mapping.md` as part of the same task. Add a row under each applicable tactic section using the technique ID, official technique title, and a relative Markdown link to the new query file. Follow the existing table format and link-escaping style. Check for an identical technique/query entry first to avoid duplicates. Do not update this ATT&CK index for ATLAS-only mappings.
11. **Validate and report.** Check that the new file follows `templatev2.md`, its front matter and body agree, every source table is listed, the filename has the expected prefix, and references/mapping URLs use the required official sources. Summarize which tables and columns were verified for the stated surface, and identify any unverified identifiers or tenant-specific coverage assumptions. If ATT&CK was included, verify each tactic row and relative link in `mapping.md`. Check Markdown and KQL fences. Do not claim the query was executed or runtime-tested unless it actually was. Report the created file path, sources and mappings included, and any assumptions or validation gaps.

## Repository References

- `templatev2.md` is the canonical query document format.
- `README.md` describes repository categories.
- Use nearby files in the chosen category to infer prefixes and filename style. Existing conventions vary; do not rename or normalize other files.
- `MITRE ATT&CK/mapping.md` is the ATT&CK query index. Preserve its tactic sections and existing entries.
- Schema-grounding approach is inspired by [KQL Grounded Queries (CAT Agent Skills)](https://microsoft.github.io/cat-agent-skills/skills/kql-grounded-queries/). This community-provided skill is a reference, not a schema authority; use Microsoft Learn and supplied tenant schemas as evidence. This workflow does not use its optional community KQL Search MCP or prior-art search.
